basic_identification.full_title: Textiles — Protective Clothing for Firefighters — Specification (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Textiles / Technical Textiles (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Textiles Protective Clothing Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies test methods and minimum performance requirements for protective clothing (firefighter suits) worn during firefighting and associated activities where there is a risk of heat and/or flame. It covers general clothing design, minimum performance levels of the materials used, and test methods to determine these performance levels. It does not cover special high-risk situations (such as specialized chemical/proximity firefighting, wildland/forest firefighting) or separate protective gear for head, hands, and feet.

revision_history.edition: First Revision (reorganized into multiple protection categories and updated test methods)

amendment_slips.description: Established on 01 October 2025, bringing updates to the technical and testing specifications for firefighter protective clothing under national quality guidelines (allowing standard without amendment to remain in force until 31 March 2026).

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Protective Textiles (Quality Control) Amendment Order, 2024' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all protective clothing for firefighters sold, distributed, stocked, or imported in India must conform to IS 16890 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Export-only products conform to buyer specifications but are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic aramid fiber protective clothing.

requirements.detail: Every suit (jacket and trousers) conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) permanently printed or labeled, along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The standard classifies firefighter protective clothing into two categories: a) Category 1: Low-level thermal/flame protection (intended for outdoor/wildland/forest support or auxiliary firefighting operations); b) Category 2: High-level convective, radiant, and flame protection (mandatory for active structural firefighting and emergency rescue where direct thermal exposure is expected).

Category 2 suits must incorporate a robust multilayer fabric assembly comprising: a) Outer Shell (at least 93% Meta-Aramid, 5% Para-Aramid, and 2% Anti-static fibers) providing inherent flame resistance, high tensile strength, and water repellency; b) Moisture Barrier (PTFE membrane laminated with aramid non-woven) blocking liquid water and chemicals while allowing breathability; c) Thermal Barrier (FR non-woven Nomex/Kevlar quilted to an innermost lining) offering thick insulation against convective and radiant heat transfer.

Each garment must be sized and labeled based on Chest or Bust Girth (cm) and Height (cm) as per Table 1. Standard overlap between the jacket/coat and trousers must be a minimum of 30 cm to prevent exposing the midsection during physical bending.
When tested, materials must show zero vertical flame propagation, no flaming or melting debris dripping, no hole formation, and minimal afterglow/afterflame times.

Materials must provide strict thermal barrier protection: convective heat transfer index (HTI24) and radiant heat transfer index (RHTI24) must meet high insulation limits under intense exposure (Category 2 requires HTI24 >= 13 s and RHTI24 >= 18 s, with a temperature rise delay of at least 4 s).

All constituent materials (outer shell, moisture barrier, thermal barrier) must withstand hot air exposure at 180°C for 5 minutes, showing zero ignition, melting, or dripping, and maximum dimensional shrinkage must not exceed 5 percent.

After undergoing a minimum of 5 laundering cycles as per standard procedures, garments must maintain high dimensional stability, restricting shrinkage to a maximum of 3 percent in both warp and weft directions.
The moisture barrier must resist chemical penetration (sulfuric acid, sodium hydroxide, o-xylene) under pressure, and the outer shell must satisfy high water-repellency ratings (spray rating >= 4).

Each item must be legibly and indelibly marked with: manufacturer's name/brand, standard number (IS 16890), category (Category 1 or Category 2), size designation (girth/height), batch/lot number, fiber composition, and extensive washing/drying care instructions.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16890 : 2024 is the strict national Indian Standard specification that establishes physical, design, and performance requirements for firefighter protective clothing (fire fighting suits). Under the mandatory national Protective Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all structural and occupational firefighting suits supplied to municipal and industrial fire forces must be certified under the BIS Standard Mark scheme (ISI Mark). Reorganized under its first revision, the standard divides suits into Category 1 (for wildland or auxiliary outdoor firefighting) and Category 2 (for severe structural fire operations), enforcing strict multi-layer aramid assemblies. Quality teams must verify convective/radiant heat transfer indices, zero melting or dripping at 180°C, high tensile strength, and water/chemical penetration resistance to secure frontline life protection.
